name: MMCSS: reserve less CPU for low-priority work
description: Lowers the share of CPU time the Multimedia Class Scheduler Service reserves for background tasks from 20% to 10%.
mechanism: Sets SystemResponsiveness=10 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile. MMCSS boosts threads registered for multimedia tasks and reserves this percentage for lower-priority work. Microsoft documents that values are rounded up to a multiple of 10 and 0 is treated as 10.
benefit: Threads registered with MMCSS (mainly audio, and engines that register 'Games' or 'Pro Audio') get slightly more uninterrupted CPU time.
drawback: No effect on games that don't use MMCSS. Background work gets less guaranteed time under full load.
recommendedFor: Expert users on high-end systems; low-latency audio work.
evidence: Documented in Win32 'Multimedia Class Scheduler Service'. Independent testing has not shown consistent FPS gains — treat as experimental.

name: MMCSS 'Games' task: high scheduling category
description: Raises the MMCSS priority profile used by games that register with the 'Games' task.
mechanism: Under ...\Multimedia\SystemProfile\Tasks\Games sets Priority=6, 'Scheduling Category'=High and 'SFIO Priority'=High (defaults 2 / Medium / Normal).
benefit: Only threads that call AvSetMmThreadCharacteristics("Games") are affected; for those, scheduling and I/O priority increase.
drawback: Most games never register with MMCSS, so typically no effect. Can starve other work if a registered thread misbehaves.
recommendedFor: Experimentation only, measured with the Benchmark Center before and after.
evidence: Values are documented in the MMCSS task registry schema. Benefit is unproven — commonly repeated online without measurements.

name: Processor scheduling: favour programs (explicit 0x26)
description: Explicitly sets 'Adjust for best performance of: Programs' with short, variable quanta and maximum foreground boost.
mechanism: Sets Win32PrioritySeparation=0x26 (38) under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\PriorityControl, as configured in System Properties › Advanced › Performance › Advanced.
benefit: Restores foreground priority if the PC was set to 'Background services'. On a default client install (value 2) behaviour is already equivalent — expect no change.
drawback: None on client Windows; on servers it reduces background service throughput.
evidence: Documented bit-field (quantum length, variability, foreground boost). Takes effect immediately.

name: Disable Power Throttling (desktops)
description: Stops Windows from running background processes in power-efficient (EcoQoS) mode.
mechanism: Sets PowerThrottlingOff=1 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\PowerThrottling. Normally Windows lowers clocks or uses efficient cores for processes it considers background.
benefit: Helper processes of games, launchers and streaming tools are not throttled when the game loses focus (alt-tab, second monitor, streaming).
drawback: Higher power use and heat; background tasks may occupy performance cores more often on hybrid CPUs.
recommendedFor: Desktop gaming/streaming PCs. Not for laptops.
evidence: Microsoft 'Introducing EcoQoS' and Windows power management documentation. Impact is workload dependent.
